title: Agents, Benchmarks, and Embedded Hacks
intro: This week the AI world kept building smarter agents and tougher benchmarks, while the hardware side saw a flood of open‑source tools and security patches. Engineers got fresh data to train on and new boards to tinker with.

themes.headline: Agent Harnesses Get a Makeover
themes.body: **Lead‑in:** Researchers are converging on the idea of a reusable "harness" for LLM agents. Papers like Grow the Harness, Harness‑Zero, and RRSI propose distilling, regularizing, and iteratively improving shared control logic, while MAGIC and COMPASS explore graph‑based coordination and spatial transformers for multi‑agent teamwork. Together they signal a shift from monolithic prompts to modular, reusable agent components.

items.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
Controlling Collectives of AI Agents in Reasoning Space with Spatial Transformers

themes.headline: Benchmarks Go Domain‑Specific
themes.body: **Lead‑in:** New evaluation suites are targeting narrow, high‑impact domains. BRIE offers a living benchmark for EHR question answering, validated by clinicians, while SWE‑Serve provides 53 production‑inference tasks for agentic engineering. These datasets push models to prove usefulness beyond generic NLP, emphasizing reliability in health and deployment contexts.

items.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving

themes.headline: Embedded DIY and Security Surge
themes.body: **Lead‑in:** The hardware community is buzzing with open‑source releases and critical patches. CERN’s colibri VHDL library, ESP32‑based audio spectrum and lighting projects, and a modular macro keypad showcase the maker spirit, while Friday’s multi‑distro security updates and the Linux 7.3‑rc4 prepatch remind engineers to stay patched.

items.title: FPGA for All — CERN Releases “colibri” VHDL Library
Audio Spectrum Analyzer on an ESP32 Display Board
ESP32 Replacement for Lighting Display Controller

themes.headline: Systems Research Tackles Memory and Consensus
themes.body: **Lead‑in:** On the CS front, xTier demonstrates kernel‑resident learned memory tiering for CXL servers using eBPF, while Hydrozoan and Flamingo propose latency‑adaptive DAG consensus and load‑balancing for Byzantine fault‑tolerant systems. These works aim to make large‑scale infrastructure both faster and more resilient.

items.title: xTier: Intelligent Tiering for CXL-Enabled Memory
Hydrozoan: Latency-Adaptive DAG Consensus under Mixed Byzantine and Crash Faults
Flamingo: On Load Balancing in DAG-based Consensus Protocols
